title: Blood Sugar Basics Quiz
summary: This quiz covers how blood sugar works and how the body regulates glucose. It also explores diabetes, testing methods, symptoms, and lifestyle factors that affect levels.

questions.q: Which of these foods is most likely to cause a quick rise in blood sugar (glucose in the blood)?
o: Plain boiled eggs
A handful of almonds
A slice of white bread
Steamed broccoli
questions.tip: White bread is high in refined starch that the body digests quickly into glucose, raising blood sugar faster than protein, fat, or fiber-rich foods.
questions.eli5: Think of white bread like sugar dissolving quickly in hot tea, while eggs or nuts are like vegetables that take much longer to cook soft.

questions.q: When doctors say 'blood sugar,' what are they usually measuring?
o: The amount of insulin in the blood
The concentration of glucose in the blood
The amount of red blood cells in the blood
The blood pressure in the arteries
questions.tip: Blood sugar usually refers to the concentration of glucose in the blood.
questions.eli5: Think of blood like delivery trucks carrying sugar packets to houses, and blood sugar is how many packets are on the road.

questions.q: Glucose in the blood is best described as what for the body?
o: The body's main source of energy for cells
A waste product the kidneys must remove
A protein that builds muscles
A vitamin that helps bones grow
questions.tip: Glucose is the body's main source of energy for cells.
questions.eli5: Like firewood keeps a stove burning, glucose is the fuel your cells burn to keep you going.

questions.q: You eat a bowl of pasta, which is rich in carbohydrates. What happens to those carbohydrates during digestion?
o: They are turned into insulin by the stomach
They pass out of the body unchanged
They are turned into calcium for the bones
They are broken down into glucose that enters the blood
questions.tip: Carbohydrates from food are broken down into glucose during digestion.
questions.eli5: Like a loaf of bread broken into crumbs for sharing, pasta is broken into tiny glucose pieces that can travel in the blood.

questions.q: What does insulin, a hormone made by the pancreas, mainly do?
o: It raises blood glucose by releasing stored sugar
It breaks down food inside the stomach
It helps glucose move from the blood into cells for energy or storage
It carries oxygen around the body
questions.tip: Insulin helps glucose move from the blood into cells for energy or storage, which lowers blood glucose.
questions.eli5: Think of insulin like a school bus driver opening the doors so sugar kids can leave the road and go into their classroom cells.

questions.q: What does glucagon, another hormone from the pancreas, do when blood glucose is low?
o: It raises blood glucose by telling the liver to release stored glucose
It lowers blood glucose by pushing glucose into muscles
It slows the heartbeat to save energy
It stops digestion to save water
questions.tip: The pancreas makes glucagon, which raises blood glucose when it is low.
questions.eli5: Like a parent bringing snacks from the pantry when the kitchen is empty, glucagon tells the liver to share its saved sugar.

questions.q: In a person without diabetes, what normally happens to blood glucose after eating a meal?
o: It stays perfectly flat and never changes
It rises and then returns toward its starting level within a few hours
It drops to zero until the next meal
It keeps rising higher for the rest of the day
questions.tip: Blood glucose normally rises after meals and returns toward baseline within a few hours.
questions.eli5: Like a tide that comes in after rain and then goes back out, sugar rises after eating and then settles down.

questions.q: After not eating for at least 8 hours overnight (a fasting test), what blood sugar level is commonly expected for an adult without diabetes?
o: Under 100 mg per dL
126 mg per dL or higher
180 to 200 mg per dL
Below 40 mg per dL
questions.tip: A common fasting level for adults without diabetes is under 100 mg per dL.
questions.eli5: Think of the water level in a bathtub after draining overnight — it should be low and steady before you add more.

questions.q: An A1c test shows your average blood sugar over about 2 to 3 months. Which result is generally considered normal?
o: Below 5.7%
Above 10%
questions.tip: An A1c below 5.7 percent is generally considered in the normal range.
questions.eli5: Like a report card average for the whole term, a lower average means your sugar stayed calm most days.

questions.q: Low blood sugar is called hypoglycemia. Below what level is blood sugar commonly defined as low?
o: Below 140 mg per dL
Below 100 mg per dL
Below 70 mg per dL
Below 200 mg per dL
questions.tip: Hypoglycemia is commonly defined as blood sugar below 70 mg per dL.
questions.eli5: Think of a car gas tank hitting the red warning line — below that mark the engine starts to sputter.

questions.q: After a meal with carbohydrates, what pattern is normal for blood sugar in a person without diabetes?
o: It stays exactly the same as before eating
It drops sharply and stays low for many hours
It stays above 300 mg per dL all day
It rises for a while, then returns toward the starting level within a few hours
questions.tip: Blood glucose normally rises after meals and returns toward baseline within a few hours.
questions.eli5: Like a crowd after the school lunch rush, the hallway fills up then clears out again.

questions.q: Fasting blood sugar in the prediabetes range is higher than normal but below diabetes. Which fasting range commonly describes prediabetes?
o: 100 to 125 mg per dL
Under 70 mg per dL
200 to 250 mg per dL
Under 50 mg per dL
questions.tip: Prediabetes fasting glucose is commonly 100 to 125 mg per dL, between normal and diabetes.
questions.eli5: Like a yellow traffic light between green and red, it means slow down and pay attention before it turns red.

questions.q: At what A1c level is diabetes commonly diagnosed?
o: 4.0% or lower
6.5% or higher
Below 5.7%
questions.tip: An A1c of 6.5 percent or higher is commonly used to diagnose diabetes.
questions.eli5: Like needing a certain score to make the team, reaching that number puts you in the diabetes range.

questions.q: After you eat a meal with carbohydrates, your blood glucose goes up. What does a healthy pancreas normally do with insulin at that time?
o: It stops making insulin completely
It releases more insulin into the blood
It switches to making only glucagon
It sends insulin to the stomach to block digestion
questions.tip: Rising blood glucose after eating normally triggers the pancreas to release more insulin.
questions.eli5: Like a kitchen that sends out more servers when lots of dinner orders come in.

questions.q: When there is more glucose than cells need right now, what does insulin help the liver and muscles do with the extra?
o: Help the kidneys remove it as sweat
Turn it into oxygen for breathing
Break it down into fiber for digestion
Help store it as glycogen in the liver and muscles for later use
questions.tip: Insulin promotes storage of extra glucose as glycogen in the liver and muscles.
questions.eli5: Like putting leftovers into lunch boxes in the fridge to eat tomorrow.

questions.q: Doctors talk about 'insulin resistance' in type 2 diabetes. What does that term mean?
o: Cells respond poorly to insulin, so glucose stays in the blood longer
The pancreas makes extra-strong insulin that works too fast
The immune system fights infections better because of insulin
Insulin completely stops being made for hours after meals
questions.tip: Insulin resistance means cells do not respond well to insulin.
questions.eli5: Like a door with a rusty lock where the key turns but the door is hard to open.

questions.q: In type 1 diabetes, which is an autoimmune condition, what happens to insulin production?
o: The pancreas makes too much insulin after every meal
The liver makes insulin instead of the pancreas
The pancreas makes little or no insulin
Cells use insulin too well so blood sugar stays high
questions.tip: In type 1 diabetes the pancreas makes little or no insulin.
questions.eli5: Like a bakery that closes down, so almost no bread goes out to the shops.

questions.q: During exercise like brisk walking, muscles burn extra glucose for energy. How does this affect blood sugar compared to what insulin normally does?
o: It raises blood sugar, which is opposite to insulin
It helps lower blood sugar, similar to insulin moving glucose out of the blood
It stops the pancreas from ever making insulin again
It has no effect on blood sugar at all
questions.tip: Physical activity lowers blood sugar because muscles use more glucose from the blood.
questions.eli5: Like shoppers clearing items off a store shelf, so the shelves get emptier faster.

questions.q: When blood sugar is high, what message does insulin send to the liver about stored sugar?
o: Keep releasing stored sugar into the blood quickly
Ignore blood sugar and make stress hormones instead
Change stored sugar into stomach acid
Stop releasing stored sugar and help store more as glycogen
questions.tip: When blood sugar is high, insulin signals the liver to stop releasing glucose and to store more.
questions.eli5: Like a teacher telling the class to stop handing out pencils and start collecting them back into the box.

questions.q: The liver saves extra glucose for later use between meals. What is this stored form of glucose called?
o: Insulin
Glycogen
Glucagon
Hemoglobin
questions.tip: The liver stores extra glucose as glycogen for later release.
questions.eli5: It's like cooking extra rice and saving it in containers for tomorrow's lunch.

questions.q: When blood sugar is low, glucagon travels in the blood to help raise it. Which organ does glucagon mainly tell to release stored sugar?
o: Lungs
Stomach
Kidneys
Liver
questions.tip: Glucagon raises low blood sugar mainly by signaling the liver to release stored glucose.
questions.eli5: It's like a school office calling the cafeteria to bring out stored snacks when kids are hungry.

questions.q: How do insulin and glucagon work as a pair to manage blood sugar?
o: Insulin lowers blood sugar while glucagon raises it
Both hormones lower blood sugar together
Both hormones raise blood sugar together
Insulin raises blood sugar while glucagon lowers it
questions.tip: Insulin lowers blood glucose while glucagon raises it to keep levels balanced.
questions.eli5: They are like a brother and sister sharing a thermostat, one cools the room and the other warms it.

questions.q: What situation most directly signals the pancreas to release more glucagon?
o: Blood sugar rising high right after a big meal
Blood sugar staying steady after a balanced snack
Blood sugar dropping low after many hours without food
Blood sugar staying normal during light walking
questions.tip: Low blood glucose is the main signal for the pancreas to release more glucagon.
questions.eli5: It is like a low-fuel light in a car telling you it is time to use the spare gas can.

questions.q: During an overnight fast with no food, what do glucagon and the liver do together?
o: Pull extra glucose out of the blood to lower sugar further
Put stored glucose back into the blood to keep sugar from dropping too low
Turn glucose into insulin to build muscle
Stop all sugar movement to save energy
questions.tip: During fasting, glucagon tells the liver to release glycogen as glucose to prevent blood sugar from dropping too low.
questions.eli5: Like a family using food from pantry jars overnight when the stores are closed.

questions.q: After a meal rich in carbohydrates, when insulin is high, what does the liver mainly do with the extra glucose?
o: Releases even more glucose into the blood
Sends glucose to the lungs to be breathed out
Changes glucose into glucagon
Stores the extra glucose as glycogen for later use
questions.tip: After meals, insulin helps the liver store extra glucose as glycogen for later.
questions.eli5: It is like putting shopping bags away into the pantry after a big grocery trip.

questions.q: You eat two meals with the same amount of carbohydrate, but one meal also has plenty of fiber from beans and vegetables. What does the fiber most likely do to your blood sugar after the meal?
o: It makes blood sugar rise faster and higher
It has no effect on how fast sugar enters the blood
It slows digestion so blood sugar rises more gradually
It turns directly into extra glucose in the stomach
questions.tip: Fiber slows digestion and can reduce sharp rises in blood sugar after meals.
questions.eli5: Like speed bumps slowing cars on a road, fiber slows digestion so sugar enters the blood more slowly.

questions.q: Why does whole-grain bread usually raise blood sugar more slowly than white bread made from refined flour?
o: Whole grains keep more fiber, which takes longer to digest
Whole grains have no carbohydrates at all
White bread has more water that slows down sugar
Whole grains stop insulin from working
questions.tip: Whole grains generally raise blood sugar more slowly than refined grains because their fiber slows digestion.
questions.eli5: Think of whole logs burning slowly in a fireplace versus shredded paper flaring up fast.

questions.q: Why do sugary drinks like regular soda tend to raise blood sugar more quickly than solid foods with a similar amount of sugar?
o: Soda has protein that pushes sugar into the blood
Solid food has no carbohydrates to digest
Soda stops the pancreas from making insulin
Liquid sugar needs very little digestion and is absorbed fast
questions.tip: Sugary drinks raise blood sugar quickly because liquid sugar is absorbed fast.
questions.eli5: Like pouring water through a funnel versus pushing thick dough through, liquid sugar flows into the blood much faster.

questions.q: Compared with carbohydrates, how do protein and fat in foods like eggs, nuts, or oil usually affect blood sugar soon after a meal?
o: They raise blood sugar much faster than carbohydrates do
They do not raise blood sugar as quickly as carbohydrates do
They cause the same instant spike as pure sugar
They turn into glucose before they leave the mouth
questions.tip: Protein and fat do not raise blood sugar as quickly as carbohydrates do.
questions.eli5: If carbs are like dry leaves catching fire fast, protein and fat are like damp wood that burns much slower.

questions.q: You eat white toast alone one day, and white toast with peanut butter, which adds protein, fat, and fiber, another day. What most likely happens to blood sugar when you add the peanut butter?
o: Blood sugar rises more slowly and peaks lower than with toast alone
Blood sugar rises much faster and higher than with toast alone
Blood sugar drops below the fasting level right away
Peanut butter removes all carbohydrate from the toast
questions.tip: Adding protein, fat, and fiber to carbohydrates slows digestion and reduces the sharp rise in blood sugar.
questions.eli5: Like adding heavy passengers to a fast car, protein and fat slow down how quickly the carb sugar gets into the blood.

questions.q: Most starch and sugar from food are broken down into glucose, but fiber is a different type of carbohydrate. What happens to most fiber during digestion?
o: It is quickly turned into glucose in the stomach
It is not fully broken down into glucose and helps slow digestion
It is turned into insulin by the pancreas
It is stored as glycogen in the liver
questions.tip: Most fiber is not broken down into glucose and it helps slow digestion.
questions.eli5: Like the stringy strings on celery you cannot chew apart, fiber passes through mostly whole and holds other food back with it.

questions.q: The glycemic index (GI) ranks carbohydrate foods on a scale from 0 to 100. What does that number actually measure?
o: How many calories the food contains per serving
How much fiber and vitamins the food contains
How quickly the carbohydrate in the food raises blood sugar compared to pure glucose
How much fat and protein the food contains
questions.tip: Glycemic index measures the speed of the blood sugar rise from a food's carbohydrate compared to pure glucose.
questions.eli5: Think like race cars on a track — pure glucose is the fastest car, and GI tells you how close other carb foods come to that speed.

questions.q: A GI of 55 or less is usually called low, and 70 or more is called high. Which of these GI values is in the low-GI range?
questions.tip: A GI of 55 or less is considered low.
questions.eli5: Like a school quiz where a smaller number means slower and gentler — 40 is in the slow group.

questions.q: How is glycemic load (GL) different from glycemic index (GI)?
o: GL measures only vitamins and minerals, while GI measures sugar
GL measures only fat content, while GI measures carbohydrate
GI measures portion size, while GL measures only the speed of digestion
GL accounts for both how fast a food raises blood sugar and how much carbohydrate is in the serving
questions.tip: Glycemic load combines GI with the grams of carbohydrate in the serving.
questions.eli5: GI is how fast each car can go, GL is speed plus how many cars are on the road — speed plus amount.

questions.q: You eat one slice of bread with a certain GI, then you eat a second identical slice. What happens to the glycemic load (GL) you get?
o: It stays exactly the same because GI did not change
It roughly doubles because you ate twice as much carbohydrate
It drops by half because your stomach digests faster
It drops to zero because the second slice has no extra effect
questions.tip: Eating a larger portion of the same carbohydrate increases glycemic load because GL depends on amount.
questions.eli5: Like adding a second spoon of sugar to tea — same kind of sugar, but double the amount makes it sweeter.

questions.q: Watermelon has a high GI of about 75, but a typical wedge has a low glycemic load of about 5. Why can both be true at once?
o: A wedge has very little total carbohydrate because it is mostly water, so the total rise per serving is small
Watermelon has no carbohydrate at all, so GI testing does not work
Glycemic load is always the opposite of glycemic index for fruits
A wedge has extra fat and protein that cancel out all the sugar
questions.tip: A food can have a high GI but low GL when a normal serving contains only a few grams of carbohydrate.
questions.eli5: Like a fast sprinter who only runs for ten seconds — very speedy, but does not go far because the run is so short.

questions.q: Which of these meal choices would likely have the lowest glycemic effect on blood sugar?
o: White toast with jam and sugary soda
A large portion of white rice eaten alone
Steel-cut oats with peanuts and apple slices
A large glass of fruit juice on an empty stomach
questions.tip: Adding fiber, protein, and fat and choosing less-refined grains slows digestion and lowers the glycemic response.
questions.eli5: Like cooking on low heat with a lid on — fiber, nuts, and whole grains put the brakes on so sugar enters the blood more slowly.

questions.q: A person with diabetes feels suddenly shaky, sweaty, and very hungry a few hours after taking insulin. Which condition do these early signs most likely point to?
o: High blood sugar (hyperglycemia), when there is too much glucose in the blood
Dehydration, when the body does not have enough water
Low blood sugar (hypoglycemia), when there is not enough glucose to fuel cells
A stomach bug from spoiled food
questions.tip: Shakiness, sweating, and sudden hunger are classic early warning signs of low blood sugar.
questions.eli5: Like a car sputtering when the gas tank is almost empty, the body shakes and rumbles when it needs fuel.

questions.q: When blood sugar drops low, many people get shaky hands, a pounding heartbeat, and nervous sweating together. What causes this alarm reaction?
o: The body releases alert hormones such as adrenaline because fuel is low
The kidneys make extra urine to remove sugar
The stomach stops digesting carbohydrates
The liver stores extra water and salt
questions.tip: Low glucose triggers adrenaline release, which causes shaking, sweating, and a fast heartbeat.
questions.eli5: Like a fire alarm ringing when there is smoke, adrenaline rings the body's alarm when sugar runs low.

questions.q: The brain needs a steady supply of glucose to work well. Which group of symptoms best shows the brain is running low on sugar during hypoglycemia (low blood sugar)?
o: Strong thirst and needing to urinate often
Warm skin and feeling full after eating
Steady energy and clear thinking
Confusion, trouble concentrating, headache, and blurry vision
questions.tip: When the brain lacks glucose, thinking, vision, and coordination suffer.
questions.eli5: Like a phone dimming and glitching on 1% battery, the brain gets fuzzy without enough sugar power.

questions.q: Maria takes medicine that lowers blood sugar in the morning, then skips lunch. In the afternoon she feels dizzy, irritable, weak, and very hungry. What is the most likely explanation?
o: Her blood sugar is rising slowly from fiber in her breakfast
Her blood sugar has dropped too low because no food replaced the glucose that was used
Her blood sugar is high from drinking too little water
Her long-term A1c average changed within one hour
questions.tip: Skipping meals after glucose-lowering medicine can cause blood sugar to fall too low.
questions.eli5: Like spending money with no paycheck coming in, using up sugar without eating leaves the account empty.

questions.q: Which symptom is more typical of high blood sugar (hyperglycemia) than of low blood sugar (hypoglycemia)?
o: Sudden shakiness or trembling hands
Extreme thirst with frequent urination
Sudden cold sweating
Sudden intense hunger
questions.tip: Extreme thirst and frequent urination are typical of high blood sugar, not low blood sugar.
questions.eli5: Like an overflowing sink that keeps needing mopping and refilling, extra sugar spills into urine and makes you very thirsty.

questions.q: Which signs suggest low blood sugar has become severe and the person needs urgent help from others?
o: Mild hunger that eases quickly
Slight thirst after a salty snack
Calm mood with clear thinking
Slurred speech, clumsiness, extreme sleepiness, or fainting
questions.tip: Severe low blood sugar impairs the brain and can cause slurred speech, clumsiness, drowsiness, or loss of consciousness.
questions.eli5: Like a laptop shutting down when the battery dies, the brain starts to shut down and the person cannot think or move right.

questions.q: Hyperglycemia means high blood sugar. Which group of early signs fits hyperglycemia best?
o: Shakiness, sweating, and sudden hunger that comes on quickly
Increased thirst, urinating often, and feeling tired
Fever, cough, and sore throat with body aches
Sudden sweating and confusion that improves after eating sugar
questions.tip: Hyperglycemia commonly causes increased thirst, frequent urination, and fatigue.
questions.eli5: Think of extra sugar like extra salt in soup — your body tries to flush it with water, so you pee more and get thirsty.

questions.q: When blood sugar stays high, why does a person often need to urinate more often?
o: The pancreas releases extra water to wash sugar out of the blood
The liver turns extra blood sugar directly into urine
High sugar makes the bladder muscles squeeze more often on their own
The kidneys spill extra glucose into the urine, and extra water leaves with it
questions.tip: In hyperglycemia the kidneys excrete excess glucose in urine, pulling water with it and increasing urination.
questions.eli5: Like sugar spilled on a wet counter drags more water when you wipe it, extra sugar in urine drags water along.

questions.q: Why do people with ongoing high blood sugar often feel very thirsty with a dry mouth?
o: Losing extra fluid through frequent urination causes dehydration and thirst
High blood sugar makes the stomach produce extra acid that dries the mouth
Sweating from low blood sugar dries out the mouth very quickly
Extra insulin in the blood absorbs water from the mouth tissues
questions.tip: Fluid loss from frequent urination in hyperglycemia leads to dehydration, thirst, and dry mouth.
questions.eli5: Like losing water from a leaky bucket, peeing out extra fluid leaves you empty and thirsty for a refill.

questions.q: A person with high blood sugar has plenty of glucose in the blood but still feels tired and weak. Why?
o: Extra glucose thickens the blood so the heart beats too slowly
Extra glucose is used up too fast by muscles, leaving no energy
Without enough effective insulin, glucose stays in the blood instead of entering cells for energy
Extra glucose blocks oxygen from reaching the brain during the day
questions.tip: Fatigue in hyperglycemia happens because glucose remains in the blood rather than entering cells for energy when insulin is lacking or not working well.
questions.eli5: Like groceries stuck on the porch with a locked front door, sugar stuck in the blood cannot get inside cells to fuel them.

questions.q: Which eyesight change can happen when blood sugar stays high for days?
o: Seeing only at night and not during the day
Needing brighter light because the pupils shrink permanently
Losing side vision with eye pain that never changes
Blurry vision that often improves as blood sugar returns toward its usual range
questions.tip: High blood sugar can cause temporary blurry vision from fluid shifts in the eye's lens.
questions.eli5: Like looking through watery plastic wrap, a swollen lens bends light the wrong way until fluid levels settle.

questions.q: Which group of signs with very high blood sugar is a warning of a serious emergency and needs urgent medical care?
o: Nausea, vomiting, belly pain, fruity-smelling breath, and confusion
Mild thirst and needing to urinate once extra at night
Slight hunger before lunch and brief tiredness after a big meal
Dry skin in winter and needing water after salty food
questions.tip: Very high blood sugar with nausea, vomiting, belly pain, fruity breath, rapid breathing, or confusion can signal diabetic ketoacidosis and needs emergency care.
questions.eli5: Like a smoke alarm plus the smell of smoke means call for help fast, those combined warning signs mean get medical help right away.

questions.q: Lena has type 1 diabetes, which means her pancreas makes little or no insulin. What does this mean for managing her blood sugar day to day?
o: She can manage it by drinking extra water alone with no medicine
She needs insulin every day, usually by shot or pump, because her body does not make it
She only needs one insulin shot per year like a vaccine
She needs no medicine if she avoids all protein and fat
questions.tip: Type 1 diabetes requires lifelong daily insulin because the body makes little or no insulin on its own.
questions.eli5: Like a phone with a dead battery that needs a charger every day, her body needs insulin from outside every day to work.

questions.q: What causes type 1 diabetes inside the body?
o: Muscles slowly stop responding to insulin after many years
The liver stores too much glycogen and blocks insulin from working
Eating a lot of sugar at once destroys the pancreas overnight
The immune system mistakenly attacks and destroys the insulin-making cells in the pancreas
questions.tip: Type 1 diabetes is an autoimmune condition where the immune system destroys pancreatic cells that make insulin.
questions.eli5: It is like security guards in a building mistakenly breaking the kitchen, so no meals can be made anymore.

questions.q: How is type 1 diabetes different from type 2 diabetes?
o: In type 1 the body makes little or no insulin from the start; in type 2 the body resists insulin and slowly makes less over time
In type 1 the body makes too much insulin; in type 2 the body makes no glucagon
In type 1 only blood sugar after meals is high; in type 2 only fasting sugar is high
In type 1 the liver makes insulin; in type 2 the pancreas makes glucagon
questions.tip: Type 1 is mainly lack of insulin from autoimmune damage, while type 2 is mainly insulin resistance with gradual loss of insulin.
questions.eli5: Type 1 is like a factory that closed down, while type 2 is like doors with rusty locks plus a factory slowing down.

questions.q: Without enough insulin, glucose stays in the blood and cannot move into cells well for energy. How does the body try to get energy, and what is the risk in type 1 diabetes?
o: It stores extra water, which safely lowers blood sugar with no risk
It makes extra insulin on its own, which quickly fixes the problem
It burns a lot of fat for energy, which can make harmful acids called ketones build up
It turns glucose into fiber, which blocks digestion completely
questions.tip: Without insulin, cells starve and the body burns fat rapidly, which can cause a dangerous buildup of ketones.
questions.eli5: Like burning scrap wood when the gas is cut off, the smoky buildup from burning fat can poison the house.

questions.q: A friend tells a teen with type 1 diabetes that cutting out all sugar and exercising a lot will cure it so insulin is no longer needed. What is true?
o: Healthy eating and activity help control blood sugar but cannot replace insulin because the body still makes little or no insulin
Cutting out sugar regrows the insulin-making cells within a few weeks
Exercise replaces insulin completely if done every morning
Skipping carbohydrates cures the autoimmune attack permanently
questions.tip: Lifestyle habits help manage type 1 diabetes but cannot cure it or replace daily insulin.
questions.eli5: Like steering and brakes help drive safely, but a car with no fuel still needs fuel to run.

questions.q: Which statement about who gets type 1 diabetes is most accurate?
o: It only happens in older adults who have extra weight
It is caused by eating too many sweets as a child
It only happens if a parent has type 2 diabetes
It often starts in childhood or the teen years but can start at any age and is not caused by lifestyle alone
questions.tip: Type 1 diabetes often begins in youth but can occur at any age and is autoimmune, not caused by diet or weight alone.
questions.eli5: Like a storm that often comes in spring but can happen any season, it can start at any age.

questions.q: Type 2 diabetes involves two related problems with insulin. What are they?
o: The immune system quickly destroys all insulin-making cells so no insulin is made
The liver stops storing any sugar and only too much glucagon is made
Body cells respond poorly to insulin, and over time the pancreas cannot make enough extra insulin
Insulin works too well so blood sugar is always too low
questions.tip: Type 2 diabetes involves insulin resistance plus gradual loss of enough insulin production.
questions.eli5: Like a key that gets rusty in the lock, then the key-maker gets tired from making extra copies.

questions.q: Which combination of factors most raises a person's chance of developing type 2 diabetes?
o: Having extra body weight, being inactive, and having close family members with type 2 diabetes
Being very active, eating high-fiber foods, and keeping a healthy weight
Having plenty of sleep and drinking only water every day
Having type 1 diabetes as a child and taking insulin shots
questions.tip: Extra weight, little activity, family history, and older age raise the risk of type 2 diabetes.
questions.eli5: Like carrying a heavy backpack every day while rarely exercising, it wears the body out faster.

questions.q: Type 2 diabetes often develops slowly over years. What does that mean for early symptoms?
o: Severe shaking, sweating, and confusion within minutes after eating sugar
Sudden high fever and skin rash that go away in a day
Sharp stomach pain right after one high-sugar drink
Mild thirst, needing to pee often, feeling tired, and cuts healing slowly
questions.tip: Early type 2 diabetes often causes mild high-blood-sugar signs like thirst, frequent urination, and fatigue.
questions.eli5: Like a slow faucet leak, you may not notice at first until the sink starts to fill.

questions.q: Why do walking after meals, healthy eating, and losing extra weight help control blood sugar in type 2 diabetes?
o: Exercise stops the pancreas from making any insulin so sugar stays in the blood
Active muscles use more blood glucose and body cells respond better to insulin
Weight loss makes the liver release extra sugar all day to keep energy high
Healthy eating removes all carbohydrates so blood sugar can never rise
questions.tip: Physical activity lowers blood sugar by increasing glucose use by muscles and improving insulin response.
questions.eli5: Like opening more doors to a busy store so shoppers get inside faster and the line outside shrinks.

questions.q: How is early treatment for type 2 diabetes often different from treatment for type 1 diabetes?
o: Healthy eating, activity, and sometimes medicines that help insulin work better, with insulin shots not always needed at first
Insulin shots are always required from day one and lifestyle changes do not help
No treatment is needed because type 2 always goes away on its own in weeks
Only sugary drinks are used to raise blood sugar back to normal
questions.tip: Type 2 is often first managed with lifestyle changes and medicines that improve insulin response, while type 1 always needs insulin.
questions.eli5: Like fixing a sticky door by cleaning the hinges first before buying a whole new door.

questions.q: If type 2 diabetes stays high and unmanaged for many years, which health problems are most likely?
o: Stronger bones and sharper eyesight within a few months
Only brief low blood sugar with no long-term effects
Higher chance of damage to the eyes, kidneys, nerves, and heart over years
The pancreas heals completely and diabetes disappears without care
questions.tip: Long-term untreated high blood sugar can damage the eyes, kidneys, nerves, and heart.
questions.eli5: Like sugary water left in pipes for years, it slowly rusts and clogs the whole system.

questions.q: You are told you have prediabetes. What does that mean about your blood sugar levels?
o: Your blood sugar is higher than normal but still below the level used to diagnose diabetes
Your blood sugar is lower than normal and you need sugar right away
Your blood sugar is already in the diabetes range and cannot change
Your blood sugar is always normal and will never rise
questions.tip: Prediabetes means blood sugar is above normal but below the diabetes threshold.
questions.eli5: Like a yellow traffic light between green and red, prediabetes is a warning zone before diabetes.

questions.q: Which hemoglobin A1c result, which shows average blood sugar over 2 to 3 months, is commonly in the prediabetes range?
o: 4.8 percent
5.2 percent
